idiom_name: js.PullSubscribe(..., nats.Durable(name), nats.DeliverAllAvailable()) or jetstream AddConsumer
implementation_notes: Default Go realization: the durable consumer persists progress server-side and the client fetches bounded batches, which maps directly onto the pattern's catch-up loop. Choose it when the stream is the integration hub and per-subscriber progress should be explicit rather than offset-based.
pitfalls: The stream's own retention limits bound the durable consumer: max_age on the stream silently truncates an old backlog.
Redelivery is at-least-once, so handlers need deduplication on message identity.

variants.name: Kafka consumer group with manual commits (kafka-go/sarama)
variants.implementation_notes: Where Kafka is the broker, the group id is the durable identity and committed offsets are the retained position, with topic and offset retention as the backlog bound. Choose it when Go services share an existing Kafka log with other languages.
pitfalls: CommitMessages must follow the side effect; committing the fetched message first loses it on crash.
A consumer whose offsets expired resumes per StartOffset/auto.offset.reset and may skip the backlog.
